title: Chapter 35 — 'I Can Get It Cheaper Online': The Full Defence
intro: The defining objection of modern appliance retail — and the complete response that protects your margin and earns the customer's trust.

sections.title: Why This Objection Is Different
sections.content:
Every appliance salesperson hears this: 'I can get it cheaper online.' It might reference Amazon, Home Depot, Costco, or a competitor's website.

This objection is different from most because it is often true. The price online may genuinely be lower. But the price is not the whole story — and your job is to help the customer understand what they are actually comparing.

The worst response is to panic and start discounting. The best response is to use ACRA and walk them through the complete picture.

sections.title: The Complete Ticket Comparison
sections.content:
When a customer says they can get it cheaper online, ask one question: 'Does that price include delivery, installation, haul-away, and warranty?'

More often than not, the online price is the product alone. Your price includes the full package. When you compare complete tickets — everything the customer actually needs to get the appliance working in their home — the gap shrinks significantly.

Sometimes it disappears entirely. Sometimes you are still higher. Either way, the customer is now comparing the real numbers, not an incomplete picture.

sections.title: What Online Cannot Provide
sections.content:
Beyond the complete ticket, there are things online retailers cannot match.

A professional who answered their questions in person. A demonstration they could touch and see. Expert advice tailored to their kitchen. Someone to call when something goes wrong. A local business that stands behind the sale.

These have real value. Not every customer will pay for them. But many will — if you articulate what they are getting that a website cannot deliver.

sections.title: Price Match — If It Applies
sections.content:
If your store has a price-match policy, use it when appropriate. But use it as a last resort, not a first response.

Lead with value. Lead with the complete ticket. Lead with what makes your store different. If none of that closes the gap and the customer is about to walk, then price match.

The customer who buys because of a price match will come back if you gave them a great experience. The customer who buys only because of a price match — with no relationship built — will leave you the next time someone is cheaper.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating how salespeople handle the online price objection, ask:

Do they compare complete tickets — or just product prices?
Do they articulate the value of in-store service, expertise, and support?
Do they use price matching strategically — or give it away immediately?
Do they stay confident — or panic the moment online pricing is mentioned?

This objection is going to happen every day. How you handle it determines your margin, your confidence, and your customer's respect.
